sentences.text:
The petitioners in OP(MV) No.958/2008 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Pala,
are the appellants in MACA No.1514 of 2013.
The 3rd respondent in the O.P, is the appellant in MACA No.1648 of 2012.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal)
2. The petitioners are the wife and children of the deceased by name Rajan, who died in a motor vehicle accident that took place on 19.02.2008.

According to the petitioners, on 19.02.2008 at about 02.15 pm while the deceased was accompanying goods in a goods autorickshaw bearing Registration No.KL-5/T-1227 driven by the 1 st respondent in a rash and negligent manner, the goods autorickshaw overturned and as a result of which, he sustained serious injuries.
3. During the pendency of the O.P the original petitioner died on 12.04.2009 and his legal heirs were impleaded as additional petitioners 2 to 4.
4. The 2nd respondent is the owner and the 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the them, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the goods autorickshaw by the 1 st respondent.
The 3rd respondent/insurer filed a written statement, admitting the policy and disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
6. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimonies of Pws 1 and 2 and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A8 on the side of the petitioners.
Exts. B1
and B2
were marked by the respondents.
7. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.44,710/-.
8. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioners as well as the 3rd respondent preferred these appeals.

9. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Jayamol vs Subhash D on 7 February, 2025

Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.
10. Heard Sri.Domson J Vattakuzhy, the learned Counsel appearing for the claimants, and Sri.P.Jacob Mathew the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
11. In the accident, the original petitioner had sustained fracture of 6th, 8th and 9th ribs in addition to the head injuries.
12. He was treated as inpatient for a period of 11 days.

However, in this case, no disability certificate was produced and as such there is no scope MACA NOs. 1648 OF 2012 & 1514 of 2013 2025:KER:11135 for awarding any compensation on the head loss of disability.
Though during the pendency of the Original Petition, the victim died, there is also no evidence to show that he died because of the injuries sustained in the accident.
13. One of the contention raised by the learned counsel for the petitioners is that towards loss of earning, the Tribunal has awarded only Rs.12,000/-.
According to the petitioners, he was a rubber tapper by profession and getting a monthly income of Rs.6,000/-.

As per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie during the year 2008 will come to Rs.6,500/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the above circumstances, considering the entire facts, I hold that towards loss of earning, the petitioners are entitle to get the notional income for a period of 6 months, which will come to Rs.39,000/-
(6,500x6).
14.
Towards pain and sufferings, loss of amenities and extra nourishment, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.10,000/-, Rs.10,000/ and Rs.2,000/- respectively.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and the period during which he was treated as inpatient, I hold that the compensation awarded on the above heads are on the lower side.
Hence, they are entitled to get Rs.30,000/-, Rs.15,000/- and Rs.5,000/- respectively.

15. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, MACA NOs. 1648 OF 2012 &
1514 of 2013 2025:KER:11135 as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
16. Therefore, the petitioners/appellants is entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.99,170/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference.

In this case, the learned counsel for the 3 rd respondent would argue that in a goods autorickshaw, there was no seating capacity except for the MACA NOs. 1648 OF 2012 & 1514 of 2013 2025:KER:11135 driver, and as such, there is no coverage for any passenger in a goods autorickshaw.
According to her, therefore, the 3rd respondent is liable to be exonerated.

She has also relied upon the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in United India Insurance Co.Ltd. v. Suresh [2008 (4) KLT 552 (SC)] and the decisions of this Court in New India Assurance Co.Ltd v. Daisy Paul and Another [2021 (2) KHC 449] and Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd v. Bheema [2021(6) KLT 462] in support of her argument.

Manoj and Others [2011 (1) KHC 226] in support of his argument that in such cases, the insurer has the liability to pay the amount with liberty to recover from the owner.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 18. In the decision of Daisy Paul (supra), the question that arose for consideration is whether the insurance company can be directed to pay the compensation to a gratuitous passenger in a vehicle covered by a statutory policy.

In paragraph 17 the learned Judge held that: on an overall re- appreciation of the facts, Sections 147 and 149 of the Act and the aforecited precedents, I am of the definite opinion that the law laid by the three Judge Bench in Asha Rani, and Tilak Singh, that a 'Statutory Policy' only covers death or bodily injury of a third party falling within the sweep of Section 147 of MACA NOs. 1648 OF 2012 & 1514 of 2013 2025:KER:11135 the Act, is squarely applicable to the facts of the present case.

Therefore, as additional premium was admittedly not paid to cover the first respondent, I have no hesitation to hold that the first respondent was a gratuitous passenger and was not covered by Exhibit B-1 policy.
Hence, the impugned award directing the appellant to pay compensation to the first respondent is erroneous and is liable to be set aside.

19. In the decision in Suresh (supra), the question that arose for consideration is whether a person who has hired a goods carriage would come within the purview of Section 147(1) of the Motor Jayamol vs Subhash D on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77914602/
6 Vehicles Act.

sentences.text: In paragraph 13 the Apex Court held that: "if the claimant had not been travelling in the vehicle as owner of the goods, he shall not be covered by the policy of the insurance.
In any view of the matter in a three wheeler goods carriage, the driver could not have allowed anybody else to share his seat.
No other person whether as a passenger or as a owner of the vehicle is supposed to share the seat of the driver.
Violation of the condition of the contract of insurance, therefore, is approved.

20. It is true that in the above decision, the Hon'ble Apex Court allowed pay and recovery by invoking the power under Article 142 of the Constitution of India, and as such, such a power cannot be exercised by this Court.

In the decision in Bheema (supra), in paragraph 13 the learned Judge held that: "thus, law in no more res integra on the point that, if the claimant had not been travelling in the vehicle as owner of the goods, he shall not be covered by the policy of insurance.
Further in a three wheeler goods carriage, the driver could not have allowed anybody else to share his seat.
No other person whether a passenger or as a owner of the vehicle is supposed to share the seat of the driver and any such action is violation of the policy conditions.

Here, the case put up by the appellant/insurer is that, the injured was accompanying the Goods Autorickshaw along with construction goods to the work site after sharing the seat of the driver and met with an accident during this course.
Ext. B1 policy would show that the seating capacity of the vehicle involved in the accident is one person and nobody is permitted to travel in the said Goods Autorickshaw, other than the driver.

Dealing with similar case as discussed the Honourable Supreme Court held that no other person whether as passenger as owner of the vehicle is supposed to share the seat of the driver and the said action is violation of the condition of the contract of insurance".
22. In the instant case, the vehicle involved is a goods autorickshaw in which the passenger capacity is only one including the driver as revealed from Ext.B1 Registration particulars.

In the above circumstances, it is to be MACA NOs. 1648 OF 2012 & 1514 of 2013 2025:KER:11135 held that the petitioner, who is a gratuitous passenger in the said goods autorickshaw was not covered by the policy and as such the Tribunal was not justified in directing the 3rd respondent to pay compensation and to recover the same from the owner.
Therefore, the 3 rd respondent is liable to be exonerated and the owner and driver (respondents 1 and 4) are liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

23. In the result, these Appeals are disposed of, and the respondents 1 and 4 are directed to deposit a total sum of Rs.99,170/- (Rupees Ninety Nine Thousand One Hundred and Seventy Only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest rate as ordered by the Tribunal, from the date of the petition till deposit/realisation, excluding interest for a period of 317 days, the period of delay in filing the appeal, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today (interest for the enhanced compensation is 8%).
